### Observed differences

- In the later window, each of the eight activities A33, A34, A36, A37, A38, A39, A40 and A41 appears in only about 50 in 100 traces, whereas before each appeared in essentially every trace (100 in 100); mean occurrences per trace halved from about 1.0 to about 0.5 [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC007, OCC008].

- The eight activities now behave as two mutually exclusive blocks: within {A33, A34, A36, A37} and within {A38, A39, A40, A41} the activities still co-occur in about half of the traces and are jointly absent in the other half, while cross-block pairs such as A33 with A38 or A36 with A40 fell from co-occurring in every trace to about 1–2 in 100 traces, with roughly half of traces containing only the first-block activity and half only the second-block activity [REL017, REL024, REL030, REL039, REL042, REL020, REL021, REL026, REL031, REL035].

- A30 and A31 still occur in every trace and keep their roles: A30 still precedes each block activity whenever they co-occur, and A31 still follows it, but in about half of traces A30 now appears without the activities that previously always followed it, and A31 without those that previously always preceded it [REL001, REL003, REL006, REL009, REL012, REL014].

- Routing follows the same pattern: about half of A30's outgoing moves now go directly into the second block (A38 about 0.11, A39 about 0.11, A40 about 0.15, A41 about 0.14, versus about 0.005 or unobserved before), and the first-block activities now frequently transition to A31 (shares of about 0.22–0.28, unobserved before); A38's share to A31 rose from about 0.24 to about 0.38 [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006].

- Relative positions shifted as expected for shorter traces: A30 moved later (mean about 0.58 to 0.66 of the trace) and A33/A34/A36/A37 moved later (about 0.65 to 0.74), while A31 and A38/A40/A41 moved slightly earlier (about 0.84 to 0.82 and about 0.77 to 0.73) [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009].

- Distances compressed: pairs from A30 to A38–A41 and from A33/A34/A36/A37 to A31 sat almost always at the largest measured distance (5 steps) before and now spread across 1–4 steps; cross-block lag items now rest on only 1–2 after-window observations and are weak alone; within-block lags shifted mildly, with A34 to A33 more often adjacent and A38 to A39 more often two steps apart [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG008, LAG014, LAG018, LAG006, LAG007, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012, LAG013, LAG015, LAG016, LAG017, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, LAG022, LAG009, LAG023, LAG024].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that, in the later window, each case executes only one of two alternative activity blocks between A30 and A31 — either {A33, A34, A36, A37} or {A38, A39, A40, A41}, in a roughly 50/50 split — whereas before, every case ran both blocks in sequence after A30 and before A31 [REL020, REL021, REL026, REL031, REL035, OCC001, OCC005, DIR001, LAG001, LAG005].

The support is direct and consistent: participation of all eight block activities halved in step; co-occurrence and mixed ordering within each block persisted while cross-block co-occurrence collapsed from 100 in 100 to about 1–2 in 100 traces; A30 and A31 retained their precedence roles; new direct edges appeared from A30 into the second block and from the first block to A31; and lag distances compressed in the way expected when one block is removed from each trace. The volume of qualifying evidence (91 items against about 1 expected without any change) also exceeds what chance screening would produce [OCC001, OCC005, REL017, REL020, REL030, REL001, REL009, DIR001, DIR005, LAG001, LAG005].

Limitations: the evidence cannot show whether the choice of block is random per case or driven by case attributes, and it cannot rule out that this exclusive-choice behaviour already existed before as a rare variant that the two windows sampled in different proportions; the coordinated halving of eight activities together with the cross-block co-occurrence collapse makes pure sampling variation unlikely, but the finite windows leave this competing explanation open [OCC001, OCC008, REL020, REL021].
